lessons.title: The license stack
lessons.why: The wrong SKU looks like a routing bug and survives every SBC reboot.
body: A person who places or receives PSTN calls needs Teams and Teams Phone, unless a bundle already includes that capability. Confirm the bundle on the licensing page, because names move. A Calling Plan, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, or Direct Routing is the connectivity choice on top.
Microsoft 365 E5 has historically included the phone-system capability and still requires a separate Calling Plan when Microsoft is the carrier. Do not promise PSTN from memory of a bundle.

chart.title: Stack height
chart.note: Required layers for a PSTN user. Not a price.

lessons.say: Teams Phone is not a carrier. Name the connectivity option separately.
lessons.fault: Outbound fails and the user has Teams only.
lessons.listen: Assign Teams Phone, then a connectivity option. A Calling Plan is extra even when the phone system came with a suite.

lessons.title: Calling Plan flavors
lessons.why: Domestic, international, and pay-as-you-go are different purchases. The country list is part of the product.
body: Calling Plans make Microsoft the carrier. You pick a flavor that matches how the user dials, and you can only buy it where Microsoft sells it. Pay-as-you-go is also the funding pattern, with communications credits, for some voice-app outbound calls.
A user in a country without Calling Plans needs Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, or Direct Routing. Assigning a SKU that cannot be used is not a routing problem. It is a catalog problem.

lessons.title: Teams Premium is not PSTN
lessons.why: Premium is a meeting add-on. Treating it as the phone license produces a design that cannot dial.
body: Teams Premium adds meeting and related features. It does not replace Teams Phone, a Calling Plan, Audio Conferencing, or a resource-account license. If a proposal removes Calling Plans because Premium was purchased, the proposal is wrong.
Say that out loud in the interview. Then go back to the connectivity option the users actually need.

lessons.title: Resource account licenses
lessons.why: Attendants and queues fail closed when the resource account has the wrong SKU, or had the right SKU removed in two steps.
body: Each auto attendant or call queue that answers needs a resource account with a Microsoft Teams Phone Resource Account license, even when you do not assign a phone number. Tenants with Teams Phone get a zero-cost allotment, and you still have to acquire those licenses.

Do not assign Teams Phone Standard to a resource account. If you must swap, remove the old license and add the resource-account license in the same license change. A two-step swap can leave the voice app broken. External transfer, callback, and on-behalf outbound also need pay-as-you-go or communications credits.
lessons.say: Resource accounts get the Teams Phone Resource Account license, not Teams Phone Standard.
lessons.fault: Queues die after Standard is removed and the new license is added in a second save.
lessons.listen: Use the Teams Phone Resource Account license. Swap licenses in one change, and fund outbound if the app dials the PSTN.

lessons.title: Rooms, common area, and shared calling
lessons.why: Devices and shared numbers have their own license sentences. Copying a user bundle onto a hallway phone wastes money and still may not work.
body: A common-area phone on Direct Routing does not need a Calling Plan. Teams Rooms use the current room SKU, not a borrowed user license. Shared Calling lets people place outbound calls through a resource account’s number, and it has its own funding rules.
Read the current page for the pattern you are about to promise. Room names change. Shared Calling is not a slogan for ‘nobody gets a number and everything still works.’

chart.title: Do not copy a user bundle

lessons.say: A Direct Routing common-area phone does not need a Calling Plan. A room has its own SKU.
lessons.fault: Every corridor phone was given a user Calling Plan on a Direct Routing design.
lessons.listen: License rooms and common-area phones on purpose. Direct Routing common-area phones do not need a Calling Plan.

lessons.title: A license set you can defend
lessons.why: Interviews and design reviews both ask for the set, not a brand name.
body: Walk the picker in this order: does the person need PSTN, who is the carrier, do meetings need a dial-in number, is there a room, is there a voice app, does that app dial out. Audio Conferencing is the meeting dial-in. It is not implied by Teams Phone.
End with the sentence that Teams Premium changed none of those answers. Then cite the licensing page, because bundles move, and this campus was checked on 14 October 2026.
lessons.say: I separate Teams Phone, the carrier, Audio Conferencing, the resource account, and Premium.
lessons.fault: One SKU is expected to cover users, rooms, queues, and meeting dial-in.
lessons.listen: Defend a license set by separating the phone system, the carrier, meeting dial-in, and the resource account.
